approved_findings: This exact URL remains a guide to turning an existing or new Payment Link into a website buy button. Dashboard design choices produce embed code with a script and stripe-buy-button web component, and revoking the account's publishable key requires updating that embed (new raw:5-29; old raw:4-28). The new HTML example replaces the prior React example, but the prose still says React can mount the same component from a script in index.html (new raw:27,31-47; old raw:26,30-53). This is an example choice, not evidence React support ended.

The three attributes remain client-reference-id, customer-email, and customer-session-client-secret. Client reference IDs are up to 200 permitted characters and invalid values silently drop; customer-email prefills an uneditable address and invalid values also drop; the customer-session secret comes from a CustomerSession (new raw:49-55; old raw:55-61). Silent dropping is important because a working checkout does not prove the supplied identifier or email was retained.

Existing-customer reuse still requires server authentication, server creation of a CustomerSession for the correct customer-configured Account or Customer v1, and passing its client_secret to the component (new raw:67-93; old raw:73-115). The secret must be provided within 30 minutes and expires another 30 minutes later; generate a fresh secret per render rather than caching it. Those are session timing statements, not a guarantee of a completed Checkout Session.

The Accounts v2 note still distinguishes Connect general availability from public preview for other Stripe users, but the new capture replaces the old incomplete access-request fragment with a Dashboard preview setting named Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts (new raw:59-65; old raw:65-71; diff:71-83). Treat that as a documented preview enrollment path, not evidence of account-specific eligibility or a requirement for Customer v1.

CSP frame-src and script-src both require https://js.stripe.com when a policy is deployed; rendering requires a website domain, so local tests need an HTTP server (new raw:112-121; old raw:135-144). Without an existing customer, subscription or saved-method flow creates a Customer, while one-time payment uses a guest customer (new raw:129; old raw:152).

The diff is mostly sample-format and navigation change: hosted image URL, React-to-HTML examples, Node SDK-to-curl CustomerSession examples, a new Accounts v2 preview enrollment instruction, and heading whitespace (diff:1-179). It does not change the embed component, attribute limits, customer identity split, CustomerSession lifetime, CSP, or guest-versus-created-customer behavior. Other raw units in the shared summary were not compared for this job.
